item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-e7ab52e4da5781f2","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"From June 2022 through March 2023, intercommunal violence in Kwamouth killed at least 300 people, destroyed or looted hundreds of homes, schools, and health centers, and displaced more than 50,000 people. The government did not reinforce overwhelmed provincial security forces until September and failed to provide adequate assistance to the displaced.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","6B.6"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The violence and government response continued into March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the delayed reinforcement and inadequate assistance to the Congolese government; it does not identify a personal presidential order.","limitations":["The death toll and displacement figures are reported estimates.","The source does not establish Félix Tshisekedi's personal involvement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e7ab52e4da5781f2","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"Congolese courts prosecuted at least 115 people for crimes connected to the Kwamouth violence; four security-force members were sentenced to death for extrajudicial killings, eight received prison sentences of up to 20 years for abuses, and 41 soldiers and police remained under investigation. At the same time, some suspected planners were appointed to mediate between communities, and hundreds of surrendered Mobondo members were transferred for army training without proper vetting.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","7B.2","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The prosecutions, appointments, surrenders, and army transfers were reported through March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes government and security-force actions but does not attribute the individual decisions to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The source reports allegations and ongoing investigations alongside convictions.","It does not establish whether the president approved the appointments or recruitment decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9ae1011d9c3c810d","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The government reported promulgating a December 2022 law establishing principles for protection and reparations for conflict-related sexual-violence victims; a September 2023 order-act criminalized gender-based violence and provided victims access to justice; an inquiry established on 9 June 2023 investigated alleged FARDC violence in Goma and Kwamouth; and police stations, community policing, and joint FARDC-police patrols were established near IDP camps.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The cited measures were enacted or operating during 2023, although the report was received in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the measures to the Congolese government and states that the president promulgated the December 2022 law.","limitations":["This is a government submission describing its own actions.","The inquiry's findings were not yet available."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9ae1011d9c3c810d","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The government reported appointing new judges to most rural courts, training commanding officers and military judges, obtaining 710 signed commitments from unit commanders, publishing the FARDC Code of Ethics and Military Conduct, adding sexual-violence and gender modules to military training, and implementing joint FARDC-police measures that it said sharply reduced sexual violence by FARDC personnel.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.7","8B.4","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The report presents these as measures implemented by 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the Congolese government and FARDC rather than directly to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The claimed reduction is not quantified or independently corroborated in the document.","The report also acknowledges persistent insecurity and insufficient resources."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9ae1011d9c3c810d","start_unit":8,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The government reported persistent implementation constraints: insecurity hampered investigations in combat zones, armed groups wore FARDC uniforms, courts lacked enough judges and were remote, logistical and financial resources were insufficient, the high-level technical team for the national sexual-violence roadmap had not been formalized by prime-ministerial decree, and reliable statistics on investigations and convictions were still being compiled.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","3B.10","6B.5","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"These limitations were reported as of the 2023 reporting period.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies government institutional and resource shortcomings but does not assign personal responsibility to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["The document is a self-report and may understate failures."]},{"source_id":"SRC-9ae1011d9c3c810d","start_unit":15,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"The government reported establishing integrated survivor-service centers, mobile clinics, post-rape kits, safe spaces, toll-free reporting numbers, gender-based-violence coordinators, a national reparations fund, and socioeconomic assistance that reached 9,500 displaced women; it also reported that civil courts resumed handling cases formerly handled by military courts and that the state-of-siege curfew was lifted.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.7","3B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The reported measures and 9,500-person result fall within or directly concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures are attributed to the government; the February 2023 decree was signed by the prime minister.","limitations":["Most results are government-reported and lack independent verification in this document.","Some measures concern future plans or ongoing implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-de820b85b3fc5b0b","start_unit":16,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"An EITI-commissioned 2021 study found that the Sicomines joint venture had deviated from its initial USD 3 billion resource-for-infrastructure terms: critical infrastructure remained unrealized and an undisclosed 2017 amendment diverted profits to shareholders while tax exemptions had been granted on the assumption that investments would be reimbursed. The DRC government initiated renegotiations in 2023.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","7B.4","7B.9","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The underlying institutional finding predates 2023, while the government's renegotiation response occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the 2023 renegotiation to the DRC government, without naming Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The reported USD 7 billion outcome occurred in January 2024 and is outside the target period.","The source does not describe the renegotiation process or its 2023 execution."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"The 2023 human-rights assessment found credible reports of arbitrary killings, enforced disappearance, torture, harsh prisons, arbitrary detention, judicial interference, political detainees, restrictions on expression and assembly, corruption, conflict abuses, and extensive gender-based violence. It also recorded that the government took some steps to investigate and punish officials, but impunity remained a serious problem.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.10","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment covers calendar year 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates the DRC government during Tshisekedi's presidency but does not establish his personal direction of each abuse or accountability measure.","limitations":["The assessment aggregates national and non-state abuses.","It does not provide a single causal attribution to the president."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"In the first half of 2023, the UNJHRO documented 2,564 human-rights abuses, more than 80 percent in conflict-affected provinces; at least 1,480 civilians were victims of summary or extrajudicial killings, including 154 children. Armed groups committed most killings, while FARDC soldiers and police also contributed.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The quantitative findings cover January-June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report distinguishes armed-group abuses from abuses by state forces; it does not attribute the overall figures personally to Tshisekedi.","limitations":["Conflict conditions and armed-group conduct are major external constraints.","The figures cover only the first half of the year."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":4,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"The government took steps against conflict abuses, including cooperation with MONUSCO, joint FARDC-Ugandan operations, IDP protection patrols, and prosecutions of some security personnel; however, FARDC elements collaborated with armed groups, state forces and armed groups illegally taxed and traded natural resources, and state agents were responsible for a minority of documented conflict-related sexual violence cases.","question_ids":["2B.4","2B.5","2B.9","3B.2","3B.6","3B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"These actions and findings concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes operations and prosecutions to the government and FARDC, while describing collaboration by some FARDC elements.","limitations":["The source does not establish presidential authorization for individual collaborations or abuses.","The proportion of state-agent sexual violence is based on documented cases, not all incidents."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Authorities restricted expression and assembly in 2023: critics, journalists, activists, and opposition figures faced arrests, threats, or prosecutions under defamation and false-information provisions; the Digital Code introduced prison penalties for disseminating false information; opposition marches were restricted; and security forces used deadly force at protests, including the 30 August Goma incident in which 56 demonstrators were reportedly killed, 75 injured, and 158 arrested. Three police officers were detained for violence during a May opposition march.","question_ids":["3B.8","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","6B.8","7B.1","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The laws, arrests, protest restrictions, and Goma and May incidents occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the restrictions and security-force conduct to government authorities; it does not establish Tshisekedi's personal order in each incident.","limitations":["The Goma casualty figure is a reported official figure and is contested by other investigations.","The report also notes that the press law resulted from consultations and contained positive elements."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":8,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"The 2023 elections were widely reported as fair but not free of abuses and irregularities; authorities investigated procedural concerns, fraud, and violence, while government authorities and security forces restricted opposition meetings, protests, movement, and media access. No party submitted a candidate list with 50 percent women, and women and marginalized groups faced substantial barriers to political participation.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.7","4B.9","4B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment concerns the December 2023 elections and campaign period.","ruler_attribution":"The report concerns the government and security forces during Tshisekedi's reelection but does not establish that he personally ordered particular restrictions.","limitations":["The report records both provisional electoral findings and allegations under investigation.","It does not resolve the validity of all fraud or violence allegations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"The government did not effectively implement anti-corruption laws in 2023; corruption allegedly deprived state coffers of hundreds of millions of dollars annually, the finance inspectorate reported USD 60 million per month in phantom civil-servant payments, special accounts limited public scrutiny, and officials were often complicit in illicit mineral trade. The country nevertheless received an improved EITI score of 85.5 points, largely for publishing extractive-sector contracts.","question_ids":["5B.5","5B.7","7B.4","7B.6","7B.9","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The corruption findings and EITI score concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report evaluates government institutions and an agency under the president's office but does not show Tshisekedi personally benefited or directed the alleged corruption.","limitations":["The EITI score reflects implementation of the 2019 standard and is not a full assessment of corruption.","The phantom-payment figure is an inspectorate allegation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":10,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The government permitted some domestic and international monitoring and operated a National Commission on Human Rights that issued reports, visited detention centers, trained magistrates, and followed up on complaints; however, authorities denied UN access to some military and intelligence detention facilities, and the commission and Human Rights Ministry lacked full-time representation in all provinces and struggled with effectiveness.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.10","4B.4","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The monitoring and access findings cover 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes cooperation, restrictions, and institutional weaknesses to the government; it does not identify a personal presidential decision.","limitations":["The source describes institutional behavior without measuring the president's direct control."]},{"source_id":"SRC-fc1de0de028c080e","start_unit":11,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"The government maintained laws and programs addressing gender violence, reproductive health, disability, HIV, and labor rights, including mobile clinics for survivors and a March 2023 recruitment process for 2,379 labor inspectors and support staff; however, enforcement was generally ineffective, services faced shortages, fewer than 1 percent of children with disabilities attended school, and most workers were in largely unregulated informal employment.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.2","6B.3","6B.4","6B.5","6B.8","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The laws, programs, recruitment process, and implementation findings concern 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes programs and recruitment to the government, without establishing Tshisekedi's personal involvement.","limitations":["The source combines national policy with structural and societal constraints.","The less-than-1-percent education figure is attributed to the ministry."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6a30815c9b8067e6","start_unit":9,"end_unit":10,"fact_summary":"In 2023, disagreements over the East African Community Regional Force's mandate intensified. President Tshisekedi sought regional partners to fight M23, but the force emphasized diplomacy and did not conduct the expected offensive operations; the Congolese government concluded that it had not achieved expected results and ended the mandate, with the last Kenyan troops departing on 21 December 2023.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.9","2B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The force's deployment, disagreement, and withdrawal occurred during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The article directly attributes the search for regional partners and the decision to discontinue the EAC mandate to Tshisekedi's government.","limitations":["The article is based on research conducted in 2022-2023 and presents competing regional and Congolese interpretations.","It does not establish that Tshisekedi's strategy caused the military stalemate alone."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6a30815c9b8067e6","start_unit":19,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"The EACRF's political track excluded M23 because Kinshasa rejected political dialogue with the group; the force's military deadlines passed without full M23 withdrawal, and neither the EAC military deployment nor diplomatic efforts produced measurable security improvement according to the article's cited assessment. Tshisekedi adopted a hardline stance, accused regional contingents of cohabiting with M23 and collecting taxes, and publicly escalated tensions with Rwanda during the election period.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.2","2B.3","2B.7","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The described policy positions, accusations, and security outcomes concern 2023, with some background from late 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The article attributes rejection of dialogue and the hardline stance to Tshisekedi's government and reports his public accusations.","limitations":["Some claims are reported interpretations or attributed quotations rather than independently verified findings.","The article notes regional interests and M23/Rwanda involvement as important external factors."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fe7819e54f39ddf","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"On 30 August 2023, Congolese security forces suppressed a planned Wazalendo demonstration in Goma, killing at least 56 people according to the official count, injuring more than 80, and arbitrarily arresting more than 150. Amnesty's investigation found the operation was planned in advance, that soldiers killed unarmed protesters, and that six officers were tried, with four convicted in early October.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","4B.9","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"All central events occurred on 30 August and in the immediate aftermath of 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The operation was conducted by state forces under the North Kivu military command; the source does not establish a direct presidential order for the killings.","limitations":["The official toll conflicts with a confidential UN estimate of 102 deaths.","Amnesty describes findings and responsibility allegations, not a final judicial determination for every implicated official."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fe7819e54f39ddf","start_unit":5,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"Tshisekedi's government used a militarized security approach in eastern DRC: it maintained the state of siege, authorized regional military interventions, mobilized local armed groups and private military companies, criticized MONUSCO, and in August 2023 used army operational orders to ban and suppress the Wazalendo protest. The orders characterized protesters as enemy auxiliaries and authorized the Republican Guard to act in the operation.","question_ids":["2B.2","2B.4","2B.5","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","8B.2","8B.3","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The state-of-siege policy and military approach predated 2023 but were implemented and intensified during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the broader approach to Tshisekedi's government and identifies the Republican Guard as reporting directly to the president.","limitations":["The source describes legal and operational authority but does not prove that Tshisekedi personally approved the specific Goma orders.","The security context included ongoing M23 attacks and regional intervention constraints."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fe7819e54f39ddf","start_unit":17,"end_unit":19,"fact_summary":"Authorities initially reported six Wazalendo deaths and 158 arrests, later reported 43 deaths, and ultimately recorded 56 deaths; a confidential UN report cited by Amnesty estimated 102 dead and 80 wounded. At least ten people remained missing, bodies were held for weeks without proper identification procedures, no ballistic investigations or autopsies were conducted, and families were denied timely access and dignified burial arrangements.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The casualty reporting, missing-persons problems, investigative failures, and burial practices occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The failures are attributed to Congolese authorities and military justice institutions, not directly to Tshisekedi personally.","limitations":["The death toll remains disputed.","Amnesty's findings concern investigative adequacy and human-rights obligations, not a final criminal judgment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fe7819e54f39ddf","start_unit":22,"end_unit":25,"fact_summary":"Military authorities prosecuted 116 Wazalendo followers and convicted 64, including four sentenced to death, while the separate trial of security personnel convicted one commander and three soldiers. Amnesty found the prosecutions of civilians lacked individualized evidence, the investigations were incomplete, victims and defense witnesses were restricted, and the court recognized only 109 victims and ordered USD 100,000 in reparations.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.4","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The arrests, trials, convictions, and reparations order occurred between September and December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The proceedings were conducted by state military authorities; the source does not establish Tshisekedi's direct role in the judicial decisions.","limitations":["Amnesty characterizes the proceedings as flawed while acknowledging convictions of some security personnel.","Appeals were pending at the time of the report."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1fe7819e54f39ddf","start_unit":37,"end_unit":38,"fact_summary":"Amnesty found that North Kivu Governor and military operations commander Constant Ndima issued the message that prompted the operation, was informed of the killings, publicly praised the security forces, and falsely claimed protesters were armed and had attacked first. The government recalled him to Kinshasa and arrested six Republican Guard members, but Amnesty found no evidence that Ndima was criminally investigated for command responsibility.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","3B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The orders, killings, public statements, recall, and accountability steps occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Ndima was a senior official under the national government; the source does not show that Tshisekedi personally ordered or approved his conduct.","limitations":["The findings concern alleged command responsibility and are not a final judicial determination.","Ndima disputed Amnesty's account and claimed he ordered investigations."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-73c8f611a76fc3aa","SRC-62a5c4d126eca104"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied materials include retrospective reports and a 2025 article; facts were included only when they materially described 2023 events, policies, outcomes, or institutional findings.","Several government-reported favorable facts are presented with explicit source limitations because they are self-reported and, in some cases, lack independent outcome verification.","No facts were identified in the Cambridge mining article or UNICEF global annual report that directly and materially described Félix Tshisekedi's actions or outcomes during 2023 for the supplied lenses."]}
